extraction.Name: Annie Hornbeck, nee Gibbons
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want it, for she did not want to pay taxes, but the Indian Agency told her that it would be assessed for taxes whether she took it or not, and, if she did not take it, the land would finally be sold for taxes, so she accepted the patent
extraction.Buyer: in 1919, she mortgaged the SW4 of her allotment to Tom Arnold, of Scenic, South Dakota, for $300.00, and, in 1920, Arnold purchased her entire half section for this mortgage of $300.00, giving in addition $500.00 in cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: Arnold, also, paid the back taxes on her 320 acre allotment, which he purchased
extraction.Occupation/Income: her husband's only income is derived by his working on farms
extraction.NOTES: her health is very poor, as is, also, her two childrens' health; her husband supports her, her two children and one grandchild; she did not sell her place for debts incurred prior to receiving her patent in fee; she considers that she received a very poor price for her allotment; with the $500.00 cash she purchased another quarter of land; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; patent issued for 320 acres; County of Shannon, State of South Dakota; affidavit sworn December 22, 1928
